missing.item: Demonstration that the revert is not recoverable by the safe (e.g., cancel + reschedule with a longer delay, or execute earlier within the new window)
missing.why: The claim is a DoS, but the safe can cancel (L657) and reschedule, or simply execute before timestamp+newPeriod. Without showing the state is unrecoverable, the effect does not support a DoS severity; at most it is a griefing/UX bug.
missing.resolves_when: Report shows a concrete sequence where the safe cannot cancel/reschedule or execute within the new window, or the impact is downgraded to a non-DoS severity.

missing.item: Confirmation that the safe (trusted role) is the only actor able to trigger this path and that this is not an accepted admin-only misconfiguration
missing.why: updateExpirationPeriod is onlyTimelock (L972), reachable only via a safe-scheduled proposal. The README lists cold/hot signers as trusted; if the only trigger is a trusted safe action, the path may fall under trusted-role assumptions and the finding is not a valid in-scope bug.
missing.resolves_when: Report identifies an untrusted actor who can cause the revert, or the contest policy is clarified to treat safe-only self-DoS as in scope.

evidence.claim: Reducing expirationPeriod via updateExpirationPeriod reverts in _afterCall because isOperationReady re-evaluates with the new (shorter) period, so the operation appears expired after execution.
evidence.support_reason: updateExpirationPeriod (L972-977) sets expirationPeriod before _afterCall runs; _afterCall (L1009-1015) re-checks isOperationReady (L399-404) which uses the new expirationPeriod, so a proposal executed in the window [timestamp+newPeriod, timestamp+oldPeriod) reverts. The pre-execution check at L600 uses the old period and passes, so the tx reverts only at L1013.
preconditions: Safe schedules updateExpirationPeriod with newPeriod < current expirationPeriod
Execution occurs after timestamp+newPeriod but before timestamp+oldPeriod
